title: A regular function separates a finite set from a point outside its closure
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $F\subseteq |X|$ be a finite set, and let $z\in |X|$ satisfy $z\notin\overline{\{x\}}$ for every $x\in F$. For $y\in |X|$ and $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, let $f(y)$ be the image of the germ $f_y$ in the residue field $\kappa(y)=\mathcal O_{X,y}/\mathfrak m_y$ [def-weil-residue-field]. There exists $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ such that $f(x)=0$ for every $x\in F$ and $f(z)\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 0F20, properties-lemma-quasi-affine-invertible-nonvanishing-section, proof: affine specialization with W=X; induction step, choice of a section vanishing at the earlier points and nonvanishing at the new point; the affine scalar construction (old item steps 1 and 5)

proof.text: Put $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points] with the affine open $U=X$ to identify $X$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and write $\mathfrak p_x,\mathfrak q$ for the primes corresponding to $x\in F,z$. The scheme isomorphism is a homeomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes](1) and its stated definition of $V$, for each $x\in F$ we therefore have $z\in\overline{\{x\}}$ if and only if $\mathfrak q\in V(\mathfrak p_x)$, if and only if $\mathfrak p_x\subseteq\mathfrak q$. Negating this equivalence gives $\mathfrak p_x\not\subseteq\mathfrak q$ for every $x\in F$.

source.place: Tag 00ES, algebra-lemma-irreducible (1); affine identification as in Schemes Tag 01IJ, convention after schemes-definition-scheme

proof.text: For each $x\in F$, choose $a_x\in\mathfrak p_x\setminus\mathfrak q$, which is possible by the non-containment just obtained. Define $f=\prod_{x\in F}a_x\in A$, taking $f=1$ when $F$ is empty. For any $x\in F$, isolate its factor: $f=a_x\prod_{y\in F\setminus\{x\}}a_y$. Since $\mathfrak p_x$ is an ideal, this proves $f\in\mathfrak p_x$. Since $\mathfrak q$ is prime and no $a_x$ belongs to it, induction on the number of factors gives $f\notin\mathfrak q$: the empty product is outside the proper ideal $\mathfrak q$, and $ab\in\mathfrak q$ would force $a\in\mathfrak q$ or $b\in\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Tag 0F20, properties-lemma-quasi-affine-invertible-nonvanishing-section, induction step: section supported away from the earlier point closures; explicit affine scalar construction using Algebra Tag 00ES (algebra-lemma-irreducible) (1) and Schemes Tag 01J3 (schemes-lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), proof, f(t)=0 iff f lies in the corresponding prime

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime](a) on $U=X$. Its residue-field value is the image of the germ used in the statement. The memberships $f\in\mathfrak p_x$ give $f(x)=0$ for every $x\in F$, and $f\notin\mathfrak q$ gives $f(z)\ne0$. This is the required global function.
